title: Hereditary discrepancy and factorization norms (AimPL) — Problem 1.4: Steinitz conjecture

problems.sourceStatement: Given vectors $v_1,...,v_n\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and a norm $X$ satisfying $\sum_{i=1}^n v_i=0$ and $||v_i||_X\le 1$ for all $i$. Define $S_n(X,d)=min_{\pi\in S^n}max_{k=1,...,n}|| \sum_{i=1}^k v_{\pi(i)}||_X$ where $S^n$ is the set of all permutations of $[n]$. Let $S(X,d)=sup_n S_n(X,d)$. Then, $S(X,d) =O(\sqrt{d})$.
problems.problem: Prove the Steinitz conjecture: for vectors in $\mathbb{R}^d$ of norm at most 1 with zero sum, there is always an ordering whose partial sums all have norm $O(\sqrt{d})$, for every norm (in particular for $\ell_2$ and $\ell_\infty$, where the bound should depend only on the dimension, not on the number of vectors).
problems.wordDescription: The Steinitz problem (going back to Steinitz 1913, answering a question of Riemann and Lévy) asks how far a zero-sum family of unit vectors can be kept from the origin when ordered: minimize the maximum norm of partial sums over all permutations. The classical Steinitz lemma gives $O(d)$ in any norm, improved to $S(X,d) \leq d$ by Grinberg-Sevastyanov (and to $d - 1 + 1/d$ for symmetric norms), with an $\Omega(d)$ lower bound for $\ell_1$-type norms. It is conjectured that for $\ell_2$ (and $\ell_\infty$) the truth is $O(\sqrt{d})$. Banaszczyk proved $O(\sqrt{d} + \sqrt{\log n})$ for $\ell_2$ (and $O(\sqrt{d\log n})$ for $\ell_\infty$) non-constructively; the workshop remark records that an algorithmic guarantee of $\sqrt{d}\log n$ was worked out at the workshop, later improved to $O(\sqrt{d\log n})$ by Bansal-Garg. Recent work (Dutta-Jha-Jiang 2026) gives an efficient algorithm matching the conjectured $O(\sqrt{d})$ bound for $\ell_2$ under the condition $d \geq \Omega(\log^7 n)$. Chobanyan's transference theorem relates the Steinitz constant to the vector-balancing discrepancy constant $\alpha(X,X,d)$.
problems.mathematicalConditions: For a normed space $(\mathbb{R}^d, \|\cdot\|_X)$ define $S_n(X, d) = \min_{\pi \in S_n} \max_{1 \leq k \leq n} \left\|\sum_{i=1}^k v_{\pi(i)}\right\|_X$ over all zero-sum families $v_1, \dots, v_n$ with $\|v_i\|_X \leq 1$, and $S(X, d) = \sup_n S_n(X, d)$. The conjecture is that $S(X, d) = O(\sqrt{d})$ for every norm $X$ (with the main cases of interest $X = \ell_2, \ell_\infty$). Known: $S(X,d) \leq d$ (Sevastyanov; Grinberg-Sevastyanov 1980); for symmetric $X$, $S(X,d) \leq d - 1 + 1/d$; $S(\ell_2, d) = O(\sqrt{d} + \sqrt{\log n})$ (Banaszczyk 2012/13) with lower bound $\Omega(\sqrt{d})$; $S(X,d) \geq \alpha(X, X, d)$ (Chobanyan).

comments.body: An algorithmic guarantee of $\sqrt{d}\log\,n$ was worked upon in the workshop.

literature.title: E. Steinitz, Bedingt konvergente Reihen und konvexe Systeme, Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik 143:128-175, 1913
literature.description: Origin of the Steinitz lemma: zero-sum unit vectors in $\mathbb{R}^d$ can be ordered so that all partial sums have norm $O(d)$.

literature.title: V. S. Grinberg, S. V. Sevastyanov, On the value of the Steinitz constant, Functional Analysis and Its Applications 14(2):125-126, 1980
literature.description: Proves $S(X, d) \leq d$ for all norms; the later strengthening to $d - 1 + 1/d$ for symmetric norms is due to Sevastyanov (confirming a claim of Banaszczyk).

literature.title: W. Banaszczyk, On the Steinitz constant (2012/2013, cited as [Ban12] in the discrepancy literature)
literature.description: Non-constructive $O(\sqrt{d} + \sqrt{\log n})$ bound for the $\ell_2$ Steinitz problem (and $O(\sqrt{d\log n})$ for $\ell_\infty$), the best known bounds, via his vector-balancing theorem.

literature.title: S. Chobanyan, Transference theorems for the Steinitz problem (1994)
literature.description: Reduces the Steinitz problem to the signed-series / vector-balancing problem, showing the Steinitz constant is bounded by the discrepancy constant $\alpha(X, X, d)$; the reduction can be made algorithmic.

literature.title: I. Bárány, On the power of linear dependencies, in Building Bridges (Bolyai Society Mathematical Studies 19), 2008, pp. 31-45
literature.description: Bárány's survey/manifesto ('epic document' per the AimPL page) discussing the Steinitz problem and the power of linear dependencies.

literature.title: N. Bansal, S. Garg, Algorithmic discrepancy beyond partial coloring, STOC 2017 (arXiv:1611.01805)
literature.description: First algorithm matching Banaszczyk's bound in the $\ell_\infty$ case and improving algorithmic bounds in the $\ell_2$ case for the signed-series / Steinitz problems ($O(\sqrt{d\log n})$ for $\ell_2$).

literature.title: K. Dutta, A. V. Jha, H. Jiang, Near-optimal constructive bounds for $\ell_2$ prefix discrepancy and Steinitz problems via affine spectral independence, arXiv:2604.13355, 2026
literature.description: Efficient algorithm matching the conjectured $O(\sqrt{d})$ bound for the $\ell_2$ Steinitz problem when $d \geq \Omega(\log^7 n)$; also covers $\ell_2$ prefix discrepancy.

literature.title: A note on the Steinitz Lemma, arXiv:2505.09465, 2025
literature.description: Survey of the history of the Steinitz lemma and the Steinitz constant, including the Grinberg-Sevastyanov and Sevastyanov bounds and the role of Banaszczyk's claim.

problems.verificationNotes: Verified on 2026-08-25. The main claims are confirmed in the literature: $S(X,d) \leq d$ (Grinberg-Sevastyanov 1980); $d - 1 + 1/d$ for symmetric norms (Sevastyanov, confirming Banaszczyk's claim, per arXiv:2505.09465); Banaszczyk's $O(\sqrt{d} + \sqrt{\log n})$ for $\ell_2$ (cited as [Ban12] in Bansal-Garg arXiv:1611.01805 and in arXiv:2604.13355); $\Omega(\sqrt{d})$ lower bound for $\ell_2$; Chobanyan's transference (Bansal-Garg cite [Cho94]: reduction from Steinitz to signed series with $B \leq E$). The claim in item (ii) that $S(\ell_p, d) = \Omega(d)$ for $1 < p < 2$ could not be independently confirmed in the literature during verification and is reported as stated on the AimPL page. The '[Harvey]' attribution for converting signings to orderings could not be pinned to a specific publication; it is reported as given on the AimPL page.
problems.statusDetails: i) Sevastiyanov showed $S(X,d) \le d$. For $X$ a symmetric norm, Banaszczyk improved this to $d-\frac{1}{d}$. ii) If $X=l_p$ for $1< p < 2$, $S(X,d) =\Omega(d)$. iii) For $X=l_2$, Banaszczyk'13 gave a bound of $O(\sqrt{d}+\sqrt{\log n})$. A lower bound of $\sqrt{d}$ is known here. iv) It is known that $S(X,d) \ge \alpha(X,X,d)$ [Chobanyan] (refer to vector balancing problem below for definition of $\alpha$). Given in Barany's epic document. Moreover, for a given set of vectors $v_1,..,v_n$ , given a signing of it achieving discrepancy $\alpha$, we can recover a permutation achieving a guarantee of $\alpha$ in the Steinitz setting [Harvey].
